Lookahead: zero-width assertion. Checks what follows current position without consuming it → match continues from same spot, asserted text not included in result.

`X(?=Y)` positive: X only if followed by Y. `X(?!Y)` negative: X only if not followed by Y.

```
\d+(?= USD)    "100 USD" → matches "100", not " USD"
foo(?!bar)     matches "foo" in "foobaz", not in "foobar"
^(?=.*\d)(?=.*[a-z]).{8,}$    stacked: needs digit AND lowercase, 8+ chars
```

Stacking works because each lookahead resets to same position → multiple independent conditions on one string.

Gotcha: `(?!...)` succeeds at end of string (nothing follows → nothing to violate). Lookbehind `(?<=Y)X` / `(?<!Y)X` is the mirror; many engines restrict it to fixed-width patterns, lookahead has no such limit.
